deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The object is Uranus, not Pallas. The radii come out near 18.7 AU (log r ≈ 1.27). The node is 73°26'14.5" and the inclination 0°47'44", which are Uranus's elements. The four times (76.4451, 355.7472, 631.6639, 958.6884 days) and longitudes come from the 1781–84 example on the previous page. The page carries out one iteration of a four-observation orbit method in which only two observations are complete; it is a draft form of Theoria Motus II.3, arts. 164 ff. The unknowns z', z'' are the distances at the two middle observations (II and III; z' ≈ r'). The constants a', b', c', d', e', P' and a'', b'', c'', d'', e'', P'' were computed on the previous page.

(1) THE TWO EQUATIONS.
- z'' = d'(z' + c')/(1 + b'/(z'^2 + a'^2)^{3/2}) − 0.049197, with log d' = 9.9999146, c' = 0.000019, log b' = 1.0569849, log a' = 7.6349261.
- z' = d''(z'' + 18.66031)/(1 + b''/(z''^2 + a''^2)^{3/2}) − 3.604451, with log d'' = 9.7784528, log b'' = 1.1254911, log a'' = 9.9984516.
- The struck constants 0.601596 and 4.220317 are earlier erroneous values of e', e'', corrected as on the previous page.
- 'Hieraus z' = 18.77664', presumably found by trial; the trial process is not shown.

(2) VERIFICATION OF THE FIXED POINT.
- log z' = 1.2736183. Adding log d' gives 1.2735329.
- The denominator log is 0.0007474, since log b' − 3 log z' = 1.0569849 − 3.8208549 (a' is negligible).
- Result: 18.740685; minus 0.049197 gives z'' = 18.691488 (the line labelled 2' is z'').
- z'' + 18.66031 = 37.351798, log 1.5723115. Adding log d'' gives 1.3507643.
- For the second denominator, log r'' = ½log(z''^2 + a''^2) = 1.2722602. Here 1.2716439 = log z'', and 9.9993837 = log(z''/r'').
- b''/r''^3 then gives a log correction of 0.0008832 (b'' − 3 log r'' = 1.1254911 − 3.8167806).
- 1.3498811 → 22.3810825; minus 3.604451 = 18.776631. This reproduces z'. Converged.

(3) HELIOCENTRIC LATITUDES AND LONGITUDES.
- For obs II, β = a'/z' = 47.395" (log 7.6349261 − 1.2736179 = 6.3613082). An auxiliary angle 15'35" − 47.395" = 14'47.605" follows; its role is not certain.
- For obs III, arctan(a''/z'') = 3°3'5.555". Subtracting it from δ'' = 96°3'34.735" gives 93°0'29.18", corrected to 93°0'29.31".
- Adding 1°9'50" gives the heliocentric longitude 94°10'19.31" (list 'Long. Hel.': 90°51'22.00", 94°10'19.31").
- log tan β'' = 9.9994012 + 7.6923332 = 7.6917344; log tan β' = 7.6188648.

(4) NODE AND INCLINATION.
- Gauss uses tan β = tan i·sin(λ − Ω), with Ω = 73°26'14.5".
- λ − Ω = 17°25'13.19" and 20°44'11.40"; log sin = 9.4761837 and 9.5490533.
- Both give log tan i = 8.1426811, i ≈ 0°47'44.9".
- Reduction to the orbit: tan u = tan(λ − Ω)/cos i, with log tan = 9.4965705 and 9.5781349 and log sec i = +0.0000419 ('+419').
- This gives orbit longitudes 90°51'27.69" and 94°10'25.90" (reduction about +5.7" and +6.6").

(5) OUTER RADII FROM THE PREVIOUS-PAGE FORMULAS.
- w'' − w' = 3°18'58.21", log sin = 8.7622717.
- r sin(w' − w) = r'' sin(w'' − w')/P': 8.7622717 + 1.2775563 = 0.0398280.
- r sin(w'' − w) = r' sin(w'' − w')(1 + P')/(P'(1 + b'/r'^3)): 8.7622717 + 0.2976426 + 1.2789140 = 0.3388283.
- From these, w and log r follow (trial values 1.2749576 and 1.2746859; 1.2746859 adopted). Likewise r''' sin(w''' − w'') = 0.1096919 and r''' sin(w''' − w') = 0.3731458 (this one uses r'', not r').
- Results: w = 87°31'17.75", 90°51'27.69", 94°10'25.90", w''' = 98°7'57.00".
- log r (leading 1 dropped) = 1.2746859, 1.2736179, 1.2722602, 1.2706144.

(6) SECTOR-TO-TRIANGLE RATIOS y FOR THE THREE INTERVALS (Theoria Motus arts. 86–91).
- Quarter log ratios of the radii: 0.0002670, 0.00033944, 0.00041145.
- These give tan(45° + ω) = (r'/r)^{1/4}, ω = 1'3.40", 1'20.61", 1'37.70"; 2ω = 2'6.81", 2'41.20", 3'15.40".
- Half-angles f = 1°40'4.97", 1°39'29.105", 1°58'45.55"; f/2 as listed.
- l = (sin²(f/2) + tan²2ω)/cos f, with log tan 2ω = 6.7887285, log tan²2ω = 3.5774570, log sin²(f/2) = 6.3260808, log sec f = 0.0001841 etc.
- 5/6 + l = 0.8335457, 0.8335434, 0.8336327 (log 9.9209294, ...).
- m = (kτ)²/(2√(rr')cos f)^3: log √(rr') + log(2cos f) = 1.5750978 etc., cubed 4.7252934 etc.; 2 log kτ = 1.3633110, 1.3527188, 1.5003234; log m = 6.6380176, 6.6313574, 6.7836991.
- h = m/(5/6 + l) = 0.00052130, 0.00051337, 0.00072899.
- Root of y³ − y² − hy − h/9 = 0 (equivalently ε ≈ (10/9)h(1 − 1.22h)) gives log yy = 0.0005026, 0.0004950, 0.0007026.

(7) CORRECTED CONSTANTS ('Neue Werthe').
- log P' changes by ½(5026 − 4950) = +38, giving 9.9947077.
- log P'' changes by ½(7026 − 4950) = +1038, giving 9.9263015.
- log b' changes by 2897 + 3660 + 7322 − 4988 = +8891, giving 1.0578740; 3660 = sum of the log sec f values, 4988 = mean of the log yy values.
- log b'' changes by 2881 + 4411 + 8758 − 5988 = +10062, giving 1.1264973.
- log(1 + P') = 0.2983914 and log(1 + P'') = 0.2657422.
- log d' = 9.7015246 + log(1 + P') = 9.9999165; log d'' = 9.5127580 + 0.2657422 = 9.7785002.
- New pars variabilis: e' = −4.410444 + 4.459680 → |e'| = 0.049236; e'' = 3.605294 + 0.0000189 = 3.605313.
- The next page repeats step (2) with these values.
errors: Mean of log r0 and log r1: (1.2746859 + 1.2736179)/2 = 1.2741519, but the page (as read) has 1.2742519. This slip of 0.0001 propagates into 1.5750978 (should be 1.5749978), 4.7252934, log m = 6.6380176 and h. The effect on log yy ≈ 0.0005026 is under 2e-7, so it is practically harmless.
log(1 + P') new: the exact increment 38·P'/(1 + P') ≈ 18.9 gives 0.2983919, not 0.2983914. log d' = 9.9999165 is consistent with 0.2983919, so either the written figure or its reading is off by 5e-7.
Denominator correction log(1 + b'/z'^3) is 0.0007471 by exact computation; Gauss has 0.0007474 (3e-7, negligible).

r''' check: 0.3731458 − 9.1025344 = 1.2706114, while 1.2706144 is adopted. Also log sin(7°16'29.31") ≈ 9.102526 rather than 9.1025344. These are small inconsistencies at the 1e-6 level, possibly from iterative adjustment of w'''.

Two determinations of log r0 appear (1.2749576 and 1.2746859). The adopted 1.2746859 corresponds to log sin(w' − w) = 8.7651421, which does not exactly match the final w' − w = 3°20'9.94" (log sin ≈ 8.76487). The reconciliation is not visible on the page.

Sign convention for e', e'' is inconsistent between the pages (+0.049197 on the previous page, used with a minus here). Both are effectively subtracted, which is internally consistent in the computation.

results.what: Iterative solution of two coupled equations for the distances at the two complete middle observations (four-observation method with only two complete observations)
results.modern_name: Gauss's method of orbit determination (four observations, two complete; Theoria Motus II.3 arts. 164 ff.)

results.what: Node and inclination from two heliocentric latitudes via tan β = tan i·sin(λ − Ω); reduction of longitudes to the orbit
results.modern_name: Standard spherical-astronomy determination of Ω and i

results.what: Ratio y of sector to triangle from two radii and time: auxiliary ω, l, m, h = m/(5/6 + l), cubic y³ − y² − hy − h/9 = 0
results.modern_name: Gauss's sector-triangle ratio method (Theoria Motus arts. 86–91)

results.what: Correction of the triangle-area ratios P', P'' and of b', b'' by the computed y values, followed by re-iteration
results.modern_name: Iterative refinement of Gauss's method using sector/triangle ratios

results.what: Application to Uranus observations 1781–84 yielding Ω ≈ 73°26', i ≈ 0°47.7', r ≈ 18.7–18.8 AU
results.modern_name: Orbit determination test case for Uranus
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss used Uranus as a test object; details of this draft are unpublished

deep.surprise_reason: This is a numerical working of Gauss's own published orbit method (Theoria Motus, 1809) on Uranus test data, from his known drafting period around 1805. It is methodologically routine for him; the only interest is as a draft illustrating the iteration with y-corrections before publication.

checkable.asserts: the first equation's main term gives 18.740685 to about 1e-6 in log (≈0)
the second equation returns z' ≈ 18.77663 (fixed point reached)

transcription_corrections: Header 'Nro [?] Pallas [?]' is the printed ledger heading 'Nro / Monath' (as on the previous page); there is no reference to Pallas. The object is Uranus.
'6991541', '6991519', '6992292' are complements of log(2 cos f), 1 − 0.3008459 etc. They are added as 0.3008459.
The left margin figures belong to the d' and d'' recomputation (8.7269194 + 0.7858396 = 9.5127580, etc.), not to new material.
